caption:
Apple has opened Siri AI to developers of any app in the iOS 27.3 betas.
Apps can now teach Siri multi-step tasks with "app skills," and Siri can move content from one app to another.
Apple says customers get it in a few months, with App Store submissions opening in the spring.

Which app would you hand over to Siri first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 9to5Mac, MacRumors · Photos: Apple via MacRumors, 9to5Mac, NewsBytes, Tech on the Go
threads_text: Apple just opened Siri AI to every app developer: apps can teach Siri multi-step tasks, and Siri can grab something in one app and send it through another. Regular users get it in a few months, not today. Which app would you let Siri run for you first?

site_article.headline: Apple opens Siri AI to all app developers in the iOS 27.3 betas
site_article.dek: A new developer preview lets any app expose its content and actions to Siri AI and teach it multi-step tasks, with a customer release expected in a few months.
site_article.summary: Apple opened its Siri AI developer preview to all developers on November 3, 2026, alongside the first 27.3 betas of its operating systems. Apps can now give Siri AI their own content and actions and teach it multi-step tasks through new app skills.
site_article.seo_title: Apple opens Siri AI to every app developer in iOS 27.3 beta
site_article.seo_description: Apple's Siri AI developer preview now lets any app add its own actions and multi-step app skills, ahead of a customer release in a few months.
site_article.answer_summary: Any developer can now build Siri AI integrations using App Intents and new app skills in the iOS 27.3 betas. Apple says the features reach customers in a few months, and App Store submissions open in the spring.

paragraphs.text: Apple has opened Siri AI to developers of any app. The company announced on November 3, 2026, that its Siri AI developer preview is available to all developers in the first betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 and visionOS 27.3, according to 9to5Mac and Unite.AI. Earlier versions of Siri AI could act in third party apps only for a smaller set of tasks that fit categories Apple had defined in advance.

Through the App Intents framework, apps can now expose their own content and actions to Siri AI. Apple's examples include checking a delivery, booking a reservation and placing an order. Siri AI can also surface any item in the Spotlight semantic index, not only content that matches an existing schema, Unite.AI reported.

The preview adds what Apple calls app skills, which let an app teach Siri how to carry out complicated tasks that take several steps. 9to5Mac described a flight tracking skill that tells Siri which app intents to use for a given request, something the first version of Siri AI could not do. Unite.AI reported that app skills are written as Markdown files whose instructions can set the order of actions, preferred intents and when Siri should ask a clarifying question.

Apple's developer documentation also describes requests that cross apps. In Apple's example, a user asks Siri to send their favorite sneakers to a partner through a messaging app, and Siri finds the item, identifies the partner in Contacts and sends it. Users often will not need to name an app: if a ride sharing app has a Live Activity running, a request to change the ride address goes to that app, 9to5Mac reported.

Developers decide what Siri can read and which actions it can take, and they can require authentication for whole items or specific details. Apple's finance example protects an account nickname and balance while keeping a routing number hidden from Siri, according to Unite.AI.

The 27.3 betas also expand what Siri AI can do in Apple's own software. MacRumors reported that Siri AI can now complete tasks in or across 15 apps, including Mail, where it can unsubscribe a user from mailing lists and undo a recently sent message, and Safari, where it can clear browsing history and close duplicate tabs. Apple is adding Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian to the languages Siri AI supports.

Apple says developers are getting early access before the features first ship to customers in a few months, and App Store submissions for Siri AI integrations are scheduled to open in the spring. External TestFlight testers cannot use the preview, and Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone and iPad in the European Union. Apple also says features that use its server side models have daily limits and that expanded access will be offered for a fee in the future.

The update moves Siri closer to the agent model that other AI assistants are pursuing, where the assistant completes tasks inside apps rather than only answering questions. Because Apple lets each developer choose what Siri can see and do, how useful the feature becomes will depend on how many popular apps build skills before the spring release.
The next step to watch is the public release of iOS 27.3 and the opening of App Store submissions in the spring, which will show which major apps ship Siri AI skills first.
